subject: science
passage: On New Year's Day 1995, instruments on the Draupner platform in the North Sea recorded a single wave about 26 meters high amid seas in which the typical large waves were less than half that height. Such rogue waves were once dismissed as sailors' exaggerations. Physicist Lucia Ferreira argues that they arise mainly through a nonlinear process in which one wave in a group steadily draws energy from its neighbors, growing far beyond what the simple overlapping of waves would predict.
passage_b: That rogue waves are real, and that they tower over the typical waves around them, is no longer in doubt; their origin is less settled. Analyses of thousands of ocean wave records have found that most rogue waves occur about as often as would be expected if many ordinary waves, traveling at different speeds and in different directions, simply happened to pile up at one place and moment. Energy-stealing instabilities, which grow strongly in laboratory tanks, may be weakened at sea, where waves spread in many directions.
stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: Rogue waves can be far taller than the typical large waves around them.
choices.B: Nonlinear instabilities are as powerful in the open sea as they are in laboratory tanks.
choices.C: The Draupner wave is the tallest wave that has ever been recorded in the open ocean.
choices.D: Rogue waves form mainly when waves traveling in different directions happen to pile up.

explanation.why: Text 1 describes the Draupner wave as about 26 meters high where typical large waves were "less than half that height." Text 2 says it is "no longer in doubt" that rogue waves "tower over the typical waves around them." The authors disagree about how rogue waves form, but both accept that they greatly exceed the surrounding waves.
explanation.A: Correct. Both texts treat rogue waves as real and far larger than the ordinary waves around them; they disagree only about the cause.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 suggests these instabilities "may be weakened at sea," so its author would not agree.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Neither text claims the Draupner wave is the tallest ever recorded.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the view suggested in Text 2; Text 1 argues that rogue waves arise mainly through a nonlinear process instead.
